name: How do I design an open kitchen so people are not constantly blocking the cooking area?

mainEntity.name: How do I design an open kitchen so people are not constantly blocking the cooking area?

acceptedAnswer.text: Plan the kitchen as a work area first and a visual centerpiece second. Keep the refrigerator, sink, cooking surface, landing space, prep area, waste storage, and major walkways arranged so people can pass without interrupting cooking. Context: Open rooms expose clutter, appliance noise, dishes, and cooking odors to adjacent living areas, so storage and ventilation become more important. A decorative island can also create bottlenecks if its clearances are not tested in the actual room. Key factors: work sequence; aisle widths; seating clearance; hood location; pantry storage. Practical guidance: Show appliance doors, cabinet openings, stools, and walking paths on the proposed plan. Decide whether the island is primarily for prep, seating, storage, or all three. Elite Remodeling & Design’s kitchen planning can address layout, cabinetry, countertops, appliances, and finishes together.
acceptedAnswer.description: Plan the cooking workflow and circulation before choosing island size or seating. Show appliance-door swings, cabinet openings, prep zones, stool clearance, and the route between the entry, dining area, living room, and pantry. An island should support the work sequence rather than simply fill the room.
